sq.q: \(\text{State and prove the change of scale property of Fourier transforms.}\)
answer: \(\text{Property: If } F[f(x)] = F(s) \text{ then } F[f(ax)] = \frac{1}{|a|} F\left(\frac{s}{a}\right), a \ne 0\)
\(\text{Proof: } F[f(ax)] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(ax) e^{i s x} dx\)
\(\text{Let } u = ax, du = a dx \Rightarrow dx = du/a\)
\(\text{For } a>0: F[f(ax)] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(u) e^{i s (u/a)} \frac{du}{a} = \frac{1}{a} F\left(\frac{s}{a}\right)\)
\(\text{For } a<0: limits reverse, giving same with } 1/|a|\)

lq.q: \(Find\quad the\quad Fourier\quad transform \quad of \quad the\quad function\\ f(x)= \begin{cases} 1, & |x|<1,\\ 0, & |x|\ge 1. \end{cases} \)
answer: \(The \quad complex \quad Fourier \quad transform \quad of \quad a \quad function \quad f(x) \quad is \quad defined \quad as \\ F(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)e^{isx}\,dx.\\ Given\\ f(x)= \begin{cases} 1, & -1<x<1,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}\\ Thus,\\ F(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-1}^{1} e^{isx}\,dx.\\ Now,\\ \int e^{isx}\,dx = \frac{e^{isx}}{is}.\\ Hence,\\ F(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left[\frac{e^{isx}}{is}\right]_{-1}^{1}\\ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\frac{e^{is}-e^{-is}}{is}.\\ Using \quad the \quad identity \quad e^{is}-e^{-is}=2i\sin s,\\ F(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{2i\sin s}{is}\\ = \frac{2\sin s}{s\sqrt{2\pi}}.\\ \boxed{ F(s)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{\sin s}{s} }\\ \)
